newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan extends general mobilisation to face attacks.
newsitem.headline: Sudan extends general mobilisation to face attacks.

text.p: Sudan's National Defence Council has extended the general mobilisation President Omar Hassan al-Bashir called for to counter fighting in the east and south, state radio reported on Saturday.
It said the council, headed by Bashir, added that the mobilisation would continue as long as the "series of plots" against Sudan were in action.

Bashir called for the general mobilisation in January to face attacks by rebels and on Thursday renewed the call to counter what Khartoum said was Eritrean shelling of Sudanese army posts near the border.
"The presidency announced... A full state of mobilization of all sectors of the Sudanese people to face up to the aggression," state television said.

"No matter from where the aggression comes -- from the remote border areas in the east, or deep in the south, the people had rallied and will always be in full alert to defy and repulse the aggression," it added.
Sudan says neighbours Ethiopia, Eritrea and Uganda are fighting with the rebels who want to overthrow the government. All three countries deny the charges.

The military campaign against the Islamist government shifted earlier this month to the far south, where the SPLA captured the town of Yei and began to advance towards the town of Juba, the largest in the whole of the south.
Northern rebels of the National Democratic Alliance (NDA) attacked the army on the Sudanese side of the Eritrean border in January but the offensive failed to win much territory.

Rebel units further south, led by the southern-based Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA), captured the Sudanese towns of Kurmuk and Qeissan on the Ethiopian border in an attack coordinated with that of the northerners.
